## 1 & 2. Owner creation pipeline and duplicate checks

**Endpoint YAML:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`

The three duplicate-check function classes (all in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`) each iterate `ownerRepository.findAll()` and compare normalized values:

- **`CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique.java`** — normalizes request telephone via `E164Telephone.normalize(...)`, compares against every existing owner's normalized telephone; throws `OwnerTelephoneConflictException`.
- **`CheckOwnerEmailUnique.java`** — lower-cases/trims email (skips when null/blank), compares against existing owners; throws `OwnerEmailConflictException`.
- **`CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique.java`** — short-circuits when `request.getSharesHousehold()` is true; otherwise compares normalized `lastName` + normalized `address` (`AddressNormalizer.normalize`) against existing owners; throws `OwnerHouseholdConflictException`.

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allow creating this owner even if another owner already has the same
            last name at the same address (they share a household). Write-only; never stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true

## Summary

I consolidated all owner duplicate detection into a single derived `identityKey = normalizedTelephone + "|" + (email or empty) + "|" + householdId`, rejecting with 409 only on an exact whole-key match.

**What changed**

- **New `OwnerIdentityKey.of(Owner)`** (`rest/function/owner/`) — the one place the key is derived: telephone normalized to E.164, email trimmed/lower-cased, householdId as-is (empty segments when absent). Used both for the check and the response so they can't drift.
- **New `CheckOwnerIdentityUnique`** step — compares the new owner's full key against every existing owner's; throws the new checked `OwnerIdentityConflictException` (→ 409 via `OwnerIdentityConflictExceptionHandler` + escalation YAML). Wired into `owners.POST.yml` **after** `assignHousehold` (so `householdId` is part of the key) and before `save` (so the not-yet-saved owner isn't compared to itself).
- **Removed** the three separate checks (`CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique`, `CheckOwnerEmailUnique`, `CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique`) and their exceptions, handlers, and escalation YAMLs; `validate` now flows straight to `checkCityCapacity`.
- **`identityKey` returned** — added to the `Owner` schema in `openapi.yml` (readOnly) and populated by an `OwnerMapper` expression, so it appears on both create and GET responses.

**Behaviour delivered**

- A full duplicate (Cp03/Cp25/Cp28) or same last-name+address+telephone household (Cp10) now collides via the single key → 409.
- Because telephone is in the key, two members of the same household (same `householdId`, different telephones) have distinct keys and are both allowed (Cp11), which also confirms the exact `telephone||householdId` format for an empty email.

One thing worth flagging: this is a deliberate behaviour change — previously, a second owner reusing an existing telephone (or email) with *different* other fields was rejected; now it's only rejected when the entire `telephone|email|householdId` key matches. That is exactly what the spec and the updated tests require.
